public_rationale: The October AgentIF results support the ordinary reliability claim: multiple current models repeatedly fail explicit constraints in realistic agent instructions. Full-instruction success is approximately 31% even for leading entries. This supports a substantial weakness, not an inability to follow instructions at all. Earlier research shows that familiar instruction tests can produce strong results. The proposed support therefore depends on reading Marcus as describing unreliable adherence, rather than uniformly poor performance on every task.
limitations: Current evidence is strongest for complex agent instructions and open-weight models.
The tentative claim about greatest danger is not assessed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Current AI does not follow instructions very well, which is perhaps its most dangerous trait.

statement.excerpt: And the thing that’s maybe most dangerous and that, I think, captures what all of us [speakers at this session] are saying here, is [current AI] doesn’t follow instructions very well.

from_speaker: [current AI] doesn’t follow instructions very well
our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion identifies the target as general-purpose LLMs.
The plain reading is that these systems have substantial, recurring difficulty reliably obeying clear, feasible instructions. It does not mean they fail every instruction.
I use October 2026, through the post date, as the latest reporting month for this ongoing capability claim.
The tentative ranking of this weakness as perhaps the most dangerous is not separately scored.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous evaluations across multiple models and realistic tasks show substantial recurring violations of explicit instructions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative contemporaneous evaluations show consistently reliable adherence across realistic instruction types, with failures confined to exceptional cases.

evidence.locator: Leaderboard, current setting; table last updated 2026-10-23
evidence.explanation: The dated leaderboard reports DeepSeek-V4-Pro satisfying 67.44% of individual constraints and all constraints on 31.27% of instructions; Qwen3.8-27B scores 65.77% and 31.35%, respectively. Across the listed open-weight models, these results show recurring failures on instructions drawn from real agent applications, supporting the reliability reading of the claim.

evidence.excerpt: models display good accuracy on IFEval.
evidence.explanation: This study reports strong performance on familiar IFEval constraints alongside much weaker generalization to new constraints. It limits any interpretation that instruction following is uniformly poor, but its earlier model evaluations cannot settle October 2026 performance.
